strengths: The broad audit addresses an important problem for multilingual NLP: Wikipedia article counts can substantially overstate usable training resources. Reporting both document and character removal makes this distinction concrete.

Examples of untranslated content, empty placeholders, and repeated templates convincingly establish specific data problems. The correlation between MinHash removal and independently estimated bot prevalence further supports the redundancy analysis.

The downstream investigation is substantial, covering monolingual pretraining, language adaptation, and multilingual pretraining. Five-run monolingual results across several tasks support the narrower finding that filtering often preserves performance; Cebuano's SIB200 improvement from 0.39 to 0.51 demonstrates a meaningful benefit.

The paper is generally readable, provides extensive per-language results and training hyperparameters, and links an open-source toolkit. Its empirical contribution is relevant even without introducing a new filtering algorithm.
weaknesses: The central quality taxonomy is insufficiently validated. Removal rates measure susceptibility to particular filters, rather than establishing general linguistic quality. Appendix A explicitly confirms that script filtering deletes foreign-script names and references, while templated articles can contain useful distinct information. Conversely, same-script language contamination remains undetected. A stratified audit of retained and removed material is needed to quantify these errors. Correlations with related proxies, including the modest DEPTH+ correlation of 0.31, do not resolve this construct-validity concern.

The multilingual BELEBELE experiment is largely uninformative: Table 14 reports average accuracy of 0.25 for both conditions, matching chance on this four-choice task. Even English scores only 0.25–0.26. Similar performance under these circumstances cannot establish preserved reading-comprehension capability. The evaluation needs diagnosis and a demonstrated functioning baseline before Figure 5 can support the stated interpretation.

The controls do not isolate the claimed effect of removing low-quality content. Appendix C uses different tokenizers for raw and filtered models, and the monolingual random baseline matches article counts rather than token volume. Because filtering disproportionately removes short articles, these conditions can contain substantially different amounts of training text. Epoch-based training also changes optimization budgets. These comparisons are useful as pipeline evaluations, but stronger causal claims require controls for tokenizer, token exposure, and individual filtering stages.

The interpretation of downstream differences is too strong. Treating differences within ±0.05 as negligible is not an equivalence test. Table 7 shows no average improvement in any quality tier, while multilingual XNLI decreases from 0.44 to 0.43 on average. BELEBELE results lack reported run variability. The evidence supports task-dependent preservation and occasional gains more clearly than a general advantage for lower-quality tiers.

Reproducibility and ranking stability remain incomplete in the manuscript. It does not specify the Wikipedia snapshot and extraction procedure, essential MinHash representation and hashing settings, or sufficiently precise clustering configuration. Four tiers are selected through iterations and manual inspection without sensitivity analysis. The code link helps, but the reported taxonomy needs a versioned configuration and evidence that its assignments survive reasonable parameter changes. These unresolved validation issues prevent a clear Findings recommendation.
